While Loop.explanation: Try expressing this loop with map, filter, fold, or recursion. Choose the approach that fits the result you want, and keep the same stopping condition and any other behavior your code relies on.

For Loop.explanation: Consider using a collection operation or recursion to express the result of this loop. Check that the new version keeps any other behavior your code relies on.

Predefined Constants.title: Predefined Constants
Predefined Constants.explanation: You can use a predefined Vector2 constant here. Its name makes the direction or zero vector easier to recognize.

Vector2 Multiplied by Zero.title: Vector2 Multiplied by Zero
Vector2 Multiplied by Zero.explanation: This rule matches a Vector2 expression multiplied by zero, on either side. Review the rewrite in the assignment’s vector model. Replacing the expression also removes evaluation of the vector operand; do not assume this is appropriate for effectful operands or every numeric model.

Placeholder Syntax (single param).title: Placeholder Syntax (single param)
Placeholder Syntax (single param).explanation: You may be able to use _ in place of the parameter name. Check that the parameter is used once and that _ still refers to the same input, especially inside nested expressions.

Placeholder Syntax (two params).title: Placeholder Syntax (two params)
Placeholder Syntax (two params).explanation: You may be able to use underscores for the two parameters. Check that each parameter is used once, in the original order, and that the types still fit.

Expand Map to Match.title: Expand Map to Match
Expand Map to Match.explanation: To practice recursion, try writing this map with an empty list case and a head :: tail case. Return Nil for the empty list, then transform the head and recurse on the tail. This version can use more stack space.

Simplify Match.title: Simplify Match
Simplify Match.explanation: You do not use the value named in this Some case. You can replace its name with _ and keep the rest of the match unchanged.

Simplify Match with If Guard.title: Simplify Match with If Guard
Simplify Match with If Guard.explanation: You do not use the value named in this Some case, either in the condition or in the body. You can replace its name with _ and keep the condition and remaining cases.

Int Ascription Eq.title: Int Ascription Eq
Int Ascription Eq.explanation: You may be able to leave out the explicit Int types in this comparison. Check that Scala still infers the types you intend and that the comparison behaves the same way.

List Ascription Eq.title: List Ascription Eq
List Ascription Eq.explanation: You may be able to leave out the explicit List types in this comparison. Check that Scala still infers the list and element types you intend.

Implicit to Using.title: Implicit to Using
Implicit to Using.explanation: In Scala 3, you can write this parameter list with using. Keep the parameter names, types, and function body the same.

Fully Qualified None.title: Fully Qualified None
Fully Qualified None.explanation: This semantic matching example identifies scala.None in its configured package. Review the rewrite’s replacement with Option.empty and its inferred type in context.

Fully Qualified List Apply.title: Fully Qualified List Apply
Fully Qualified List Apply.explanation: This example matches the specific List(1, 2) construction by its fully qualified symbol. Use Vector(1, 2) only where changing the concrete collection type fits the exercise. This is not a general recommendation to replace every List.

Fully Qualified String.title: Fully Qualified String
Fully Qualified String.explanation: This example matches java.lang.String within its configured package. The configured replacement is also java.lang.String. A match may produce no textual change.

Fully Qualified Option.title: Fully Qualified Option
Fully Qualified Option.explanation: This example matches scala.Option within its configured package. The configured replacement is also scala.Option. A match may produce no textual change.

BracketMigration.title: BracketMigration
BracketMigration.explanation: This rule matches Stream.bracket with acquire, use and release argument groups. Apply the rewrite’s bracket(acquire)(release).flatMap(use) form only for the API version targeted by this migration.

DebounceMigration.title: DebounceMigration
DebounceMigration.explanation: This rule matches a stream passed through a Scheduler debounce operation. Use src.debounce(d) for the API version targeted by this migration and check the surrounding timing context.

SchedulerToTimer.title: SchedulerToTimer
SchedulerToTimer.explanation: This rule matches a value declaration ascribed as fs2.Scheduler. The configured rewrite hardcodes the name scheduler and type Timer[F]. Review references, the type parameter F and imports in the surrounding code.

SemaphoreMigration.title: SemaphoreMigration
SemaphoreMigration.explanation: This rule matches decrement on a Semaphore value. Use acquire for the semaphore API version targeted by this migration.

SemaphoreImport.title: SemaphoreImport
SemaphoreImport.explanation: This rule matches an import of fs2.async.mutable.Semaphore. Use the target import only with the dependency version expected by this migration, then check the semaphore call sites.

Remove Debug Prints.title: Remove Debug Prints
Remove Debug Prints.explanation: If this println was only for debugging, you can remove it. First check that computing its argument does not perform work your program still needs.
